title: Integration and browser testing concepts
learningObjectives: Explain integration and browser testing concepts and apply a repeatable software quality workflow.

understand.concept: Integration tests verify that multiple modules or services work together. Browser or end-to-end tests exercise user-visible workflows in a real browser environment, including navigation, forms, and rendering. Each test level finds different classes of defects.
understand.whyItMatters: A function can pass unit tests while the full page fails because modules, network responses, or event wiring do not work together. Layered testing gives broader confidence.
understand.analogy: Unit tests check individual tools; integration tests check how tools fit together; browser tests check the whole user journey.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; test quality depends on coverage, environment, and the actual contracts under test.

explain.narrative: The outline verifies a repository-renderer boundary rather than one function in isolation. Browser automation can extend it to real interaction.

examples.explanation: The outline verifies a repository-renderer boundary rather than one function in isolation. Browser automation can extend it to real interaction.
examples.expectedOutput: The example demonstrates a repeatable check or quality practice.

practise.guidedTask: Design an integration test for loading and rendering a lesson, then a browser test for completing its exercise.
practise.independentTask: Apply the quality practice to a small feature. Record the expected behaviour, test evidence, and any limitations that remain.
hints: Treat automated checks as evidence, not proof of correctness.

questions.prompt: What does an integration test primarily verify?
options: That connected modules or services work together
questions.answer: That connected modules or services work together
questions.explanation: Integration tests exercise interactions across component boundaries.

questions.prompt: What does a healthy testing and review process provide?
options: Repeatable evidence about behaviour and maintainability
A guarantee that no defects can ever occur
A reason to skip manual testing
questions.answer: Repeatable evidence about behaviour and maintainability
questions.explanation: Testing and review reduce risk but cannot guarantee the absence of every defect.
